To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the advanced n-gram model produces better results than the normal ngrams in terms of the task-based evaluation, while it is outper- formed by the linear feature combination approach in the context-based evaluation.

(1) the advanced n-gram model produces higher expected precision and expected accuracy scores than the normal ones, and (2) the linear feature combination method outperforms the n-gram methods in terms of expected recall, and it also produces the best expected accuracies, and (3) the perplexity of all models is very high, which indicates that they are all still very far from producing user responses which are realistic in terms of their frequency of occurrence
the advanced n-gram model outperforms other models for small values of the n-grams and the linear feature combination outperforms other methods for larger values of the ngrams.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of techniques for simulating user actions for spoken dialogue systems.
the development of user simulation models for spoken dialogue systems, which are able to capture user behaviour in a realistic way.
the development of a user simulator for spoken dialogue systems, which is able to generate responses that are similar to real users.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the linear model performs the best in the context-based evaluation and that the advanced n-gram model is best suited for small data sets, i.e. when little data is available to build larger n-grams.
the linear model is the best for the task of dialogue policy learning and that the advanced n-gram models are better suited for simulating user actions in a given dialogue state.
all methods are useful in different situations, and that no method is clearly better than the others.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the advanced n-gram user model is a good choice for user simulation in spoken dialogue systems.
the linear model is the best for task-based evaluation, while the advanced n- grams are the best for the user simulation evaluation.
the “advanced” user simulation method is more accurate than the “normal” ngram user simulation and it can be trained with less data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the advanced n-gram model produces better results than the normal ngrams and that the linear model outperforms all n-gram models.
the advanced n-gram user model outperforms both normal ngrams and the linear model, especially for larger values of n.
user simulation based on the advanced n-gram model is a promising approach for simulating user actions in spoken dialogue systems.
